stages.label: Instruction
stages.purpose: Client instructed; identity and AML established before anything is ordered.
gates: ID / AML check resolved (cleared by the rule layer, or reviewed by a person)

stages.label: Pre-contract
stages.purpose: Searches ordered automatically on entry; enquiries raised; the mortgage offer checked; on a leasehold purchase, the management pack reviewed.
gates: every required search ordered and resolved
every enquiry replied and resolved (or withdrawn)

stages.label: Contract review
stages.purpose: Title reviewed; the report on title drafted by AI, approved by a person, sent.
gates: report on title sent (drafted → approved by a person → sent)

stages.label: Pre-exchange
stages.purpose: Deposit in; exchange conditions derived; contracts exchanged with a completion date.
gates: proof of funds signed off (firm policy)
client satisfied with the physical condition where a survey is on file

stages.label: Pre-completion
stages.purpose: Funds requested and received; the completion payment authorised by a person against verified bank details; completion confirmed.
gates: completion payment authorised against verified seller's-solicitor details

stages.label: Post-completion
stages.purpose: Registration at HM Land Registry; requisitions answered.

terminal.label: Closed
terminal.how: close_matter after registration with no open issues (leasehold: notice of assignment served)

terminal.label: Abandoned
terminal.how: abandon_matter from any stage before completion

terminal.label: Manual handling
terminal.how: mark_manual_handling, ID rejected, or non-freehold title — automation stops, the log continues

subflows.label: ID / AML
subflows.rule: Provider outcome "clear" with no flags → clear; "refer"/"fail", any flag, or low extraction confidence → flag. Reject halts automation.

subflows.label: Searches
subflows.rule: Only info-severity entries → clear; any low/medium/high flag, or confidence below the threshold → flag. A resolved search may be re-ordered (new cycle).

subflows.label: Enquiries
subflows.rule: Reply "answered" with no issues → clear; partial/refused/issues → flag. "Request further" raises a tracked follow-up; a person may withdraw one.

subflows.label: Mortgage offer
subflows.rule: Standard conditions only and expiry comfortably after the target exchange → clear; any special condition, near expiry, or low confidence → flag. Withdrawal reopens the sub-flow and blocks exchange.

subflows.label: Title
subflows.rule: Freehold with no restrictions, charges or covenants → clear; any entry → flag with the register section cited; non-freehold tenure → manual handling.

subflows.label: Report on title
subflows.rule: Always a decision: the AI draft is approved or rejected by a person; it is sent only after the approval event, and the database refuses a send without one.

subflows.label: Proof of funds
subflows.rule: Always a decision: the client's declaration is rule-checked (shortfall, unevidenced source, gift, repayable gift, higher-risk source, incomplete declarations) and briefed; the conveyancer signs off, asks for more (re-opens the form), escalates or rejects (manual handling). A round in flight holds exchange.

subflows.label: Management pack (leasehold)
subflows.rule: Leasehold only. Always a decision: the LPE1 is a set of client-advice points (service charge, ground rent, arrears, major works, insurance). Gates pre_contract on a leasehold purchase.

subflows.label: Chasing & escalation
subflows.rule: Working-day timers chase the party that owes us and escalate to a person with a dossier; deadlines we owe are raised once, in time.

decisions.label: bank details
decisions.source: the document the details arrived on

deadlines.description: an open issue with no movement (working days since last touched)

invariants.title: Replayable
invariants.rule: project(log) reproduces the live state exactly; the audit verifies the hash chain and the replay.

invariants.title: Every decision cites a source
invariants.rule: A decision event without a document, a summary, a citation or an option is refused before it is written.

invariants.title: Source before verdict
invariants.rule: Resolving needs decision_source_opened by the same person and scroll/dwell engagement; the server refuses (412) without both.

invariants.title: A reason for anything but approve
invariants.rule: Non-approve options need a written reason stored on the resolving event.

invariants.title: No payment or send by automation
invariants.rule: funds_requested, payment_authorised and report_on_title_sent need a human approver; the database trigger refuses otherwise, and the automation role cannot write them at all.

invariants.title: Bank details are a hard stop
invariants.rule: Every set or change is a decision resolved only by out-of-band verification; payments are refused (423) while one is pending or against a superseded record.

invariants.title: Two kinds of transition only
invariants.rule: Actor is system, ai, external or a user id; anything ambiguous becomes a decision.

invariants.title: Walled counterparties
invariants.rule: Internally-linked matters are separated by row-level security; the same enquiry event pair is used across the wall.

invariants.title: Shadow before live
invariants.rule: A shadow matter or sub-flow is logged, never surfaced, never sent; conclusions are compared with the human record before promotion.

invariants.title: The log only says what happened
invariants.rule: I/O is recorded after it succeeded; a result that arrives for a step nobody started records the start first (actor external); errors are corrections, never edits.

invariants.title: Abandoned is final
invariants.rule: After matter_abandoned nothing moves: waits close, timers stop, commands are refused, only corrections are accepted.

invariants.title: An open issue holds its gate
invariants.rule: An open or negotiating issue gated on exchange blocks exchange_conditions_met, contracts_exchanged and the pre_exchange exit; one gated on completion blocks completion_confirmed. Everything else proceeds ("everything but exchange can go on"). Releasing a hold needs a note.

invariants.title: Facts are automated, judgements are routed
invariants.rule: The machine records objective facts from documents (a report arrived, it recommends further investigation, a specialist finds nothing) and never infers a judgement: title / enquiries / AML satisfactory are a conveyancer's decision; satisfied with the property, accept a risk, authority to exchange are the client's, recorded by a person from their instruction.

invariants.title: Source of funds is scrutinised, not filed
invariants.rule: Every attached statement is read transaction by transaction; every unusual credit drafts a query; sign-off is refused while a query is open (send it, or withdraw it with a reason); a round in flight — and, by firm policy, an unsigned-off check — holds exchange; money accepted before sign-off raises an issue; a price rise beyond the verified funds re-opens the question.

invariants.title: The lender is told
invariants.rule: On a lender-funded purchase a price change, an indemnity policy or a retention automatically raises a lender_approval issue that holds exchange until the lender confirms.

triggers.label: Email attachment filed to the matter
triggers.description: An attachment on a matched thread is saved into the matter (Graph) and handed to the engine: classified, routed to a sub-flow or reported for a person to file.

triggers.label: File dropped in the matter folder (OneDrive)
triggers.description: The matter folder is scanned (files/live, files/process); new documents go through the same ingest.

triggers.label: Upload from the engine panel
triggers.description: A person uploads a PDF and (optionally) says what it is; an explicit role bypasses the classifier.

triggers.label: File an existing document with an explicit role
triggers.description: For the reply the classifier could not match, or a search of an unusual type.

triggers.label: InfoTrack result returned
triggers.description: Signed webhook; the order record (ours) says which matter and sub-flow; the result is downloaded, filed and routed.

triggers.label: Client message (WhatsApp)
triggers.description: Guarded Q&A: an FAQ answer goes back automatically; anything else is routed to the handler. Never a command.

triggers.label: A person records what happened
triggers.description: Enrol, raise an enquiry, deposit received, exchange, completion, SDLT/AP1, bank details, abandonment, date changes, notices, requisitions, corrections — from the engine panel, the decision panel or the Outlook taskpane.

triggers.label: Client submits the proof-of-funds form
triggers.description: Public, tokenised form (no login): the client declares each source, attaches evidence and signs the declarations. The submission becomes typed facts, rule flags, a declaration document and a sign-off decision for the conveyancer.

triggers.label: Decision resolved in the panel
triggers.description: Open the source, engage with it, choose an option with a reason. Resolves the sub-flow and may raise a follow-up enquiry or an escalation.

triggers.label: Working-day timer sweep
triggers.description: Chases and escalations for open waits (searches, enquiries, ID, funds, registration) and deadlines we owe (offer expiry, SDLT, notice to complete, requisition reply).

triggers.label: Outlook add-in taskpane
triggers.description: The decision feed inside Outlook; the same routes as the panel.

triggers.label: Matter reassigned in the app
triggers.description: Assignment lives on the matter row; the change is put on the engine log as handler_changed.

triggers.label: Document filed in LEAP
triggers.description: LEAP posts a pointer; we re-read the document from LEAP, mirror it (bytes stay in LEAP) and hand it to the engine — with LEAP's folder and file name as a routing prior. Out-of-order documents wait as PENDING.
triggers.notes: Event names and signature scheme to confirm against the LEAP reference.

triggers.label: Matter created / updated / closed in LEAP
triggers.description: Mirror the matter, its parties and key dates; enrol a new freehold purchase (shadow first); a closed matter closes the mirror.

triggers.label: Card (party) updated in LEAP
triggers.description: Refresh the matter's parties: client contact for comms, lender presence, the other side's solicitor for the counterparty resolver.

triggers.label: Polling sync — matters
triggers.description: Matters changed since the watermark; the safety net under webhooks.

triggers.label: Polling sync — documents on every enrolled matter
triggers.description: Every enrolled matter's documents from its own watermark (a new document does not necessarily change the matter's modified date), plus retries of PENDING ones.

triggers.label: CONVEYi task ticked off in LEAP
triggers.description: Phase 2 candidate: a handler completing our task in LEAP could open the decision panel link, never resolve the decision (the source-and-engagement gate lives in the panel).

triggers.label: Key date changed in LEAP (exchange / completion)
triggers.description: Phase 2: LEAP calendar / matter key dates → set_target_dates or change_completion_date on the log.
triggers.notes: Today the sync updates the mirror's dates; the engine command is not yet issued automatically.

triggers.label: Email / letter filed to the LEAP matter
triggers.description: Phase 2: LEAP correspondence records (inbound emails filed to the matter) as an ingest source for enquiry replies and bank-details changes.
triggers.notes: Needs LEAP's correspondence resource from the reference.

eventualities.mechanism: reviewTransactions flags each line and drafts the query; QUERY_UNANSWERED keeps it open; risk rating enhanced

eventualities.mechanism: abandon_matter(conflict); same-handler links refused at the DB

requisition decision; blocks ap1_confirmed; deadline timer
idempotent on provider id; re-issue = new cycle

kinds.label: Title defect / discrepancy
kinds.arisesFrom: the register: possessory or qualified title, a missing deed, an unregistered part, an undated or unsigned deed, a name that does not match
kinds.note: Rectified by indemnity, a statutory declaration, a deed of grant or first registration; these are the gaps HM Land Registry later requisitions on.
actions: Identify the defect precisely against the register
Decide the route: indemnity, rectification, statutory declaration, first registration
Raise the enquiry / request the deed
Report to the lender if the title is unacceptable

kinds.label: Restriction on title
kinds.arisesFrom: a Form A / B / L restriction in the proprietorship register (co-owners, a management company, a lender, a s.106 or overage restriction) whose terms must be complied with before the transfer registers
kinds.note: The certificate or consent the restriction demands is often in a third party's hands (management company, chargee) — a classic slow item; HMLR rejects the AP1 without it.
kinds.overlaps: the title sub-flow flags the entry as a decision; the issue tracks getting what the restriction demands
actions: Request the certificate / consent the restriction demands
Check the AP1 will not be rejected

kinds.label: Missing easement / right
kinds.arisesFrom: no right of way over a private road or shared drive, no right for services (drains, pipes) across a neighbour's land, a CON29 2.1 "not adopted" answer
kinds.note: A lender may find the title unacceptable without a legal right of access; a deed of grant from the neighbour or a 20-year statutory declaration fixes it, an indemnity insures it.
actions: Establish who owns the servient land
Request a deed of grant or a statutory declaration

kinds.label: Restrictive covenant
kinds.arisesFrom: the charges register (no alterations without consent, use restrictions, a covenant already breached by the extension)
kinds.note: The trap: once the covenantee is asked for retrospective consent, an indemnity policy is no longer available because they know. Decide the route before anyone writes to them.
actions: Decide indemnity versus consent BEFORE anyone approaches the covenantee

kinds.label: Boundary discrepancy
kinds.arisesFrom: the title plan against the survey / the fence line / the estate agent's particulars; a strip of land in a neighbour's title
kinds.note: Usually resolved by a statutory declaration or a determined-boundary application later; a lender will want the land the house sits on to be in the title.
actions: Compare the title plan with the survey and the particulars
Consider a statutory declaration or a determined-boundary application

kinds.label: Missing consent
kinds.arisesFrom: works or a use that needed a third party's consent under the title (landlord, management company, covenantee, estate rentcharge owner) and got none
kinds.note: Same indemnity-versus-approach choice as a covenant breach.

kinds.label: Lease defect
kinds.arisesFrom: a defective lease: no forfeiture-on-insolvency protection, missing repairing or insurance provisions, no rights over common parts
kinds.note: Lenders (UK Finance Handbook) list what a lease must contain; a deed of variation needs the landlord and every lender to sign.
kinds.overlaps: leasehold tenure puts the matter into manual handling in v1; the issue records the defect
actions: Check the lease against the UK Finance Handbook requirements
Request a deed of variation or quote an indemnity

kinds.label: Short lease
kinds.arisesFrom: an unexpired term below the lender's minimum (typically 70–85 years at completion) or approaching 80 years (marriage value)
kinds.note: A statutory extension takes months; the common route is the seller serving the s.42 notice and assigning the benefit on completion.
actions: Advise on a s.42 notice served by the seller and assigned on completion

kinds.label: Service charge issue
kinds.arisesFrom: arrears, a disputed demand, a large planned major works bill, an unclear reserve fund in the management pack
kinds.note: Retention from the price for the next demand is the usual fix; arrears must be cleared before the landlord will register the assignment.
actions: Agree a retention for planned works
Confirm arrears are cleared before completion

kinds.label: Ground rent issue
kinds.arisesFrom: escalating (doubling) ground rent, rent above £250 / £1,000 in London (assured tenancy risk), arrears
kinds.note: Many lenders refuse doubling rents; a deed of variation from the freeholder or a lender-approved indemnity is the route.
actions: Request a deed of variation or quote an indemnity

kinds.label: Freeholder / managing-agent information outstanding
kinds.arisesFrom: the LPE1 / management pack not yet supplied (fees unpaid, agent slow), missing accounts, insurance or fire-risk assessment
kinds.note: The single most-cited leasehold delay: packs take 2–8 weeks and the seller must pay for them; chase early, in writing.
actions: Chase the seller's solicitor for the pack
Confirm the fee has been paid
Ask for the managing agent's expected date

kinds.label: Planning permission missing
kinds.arisesFrom: works with no decision notice (extension, conversion, change of use), a CON29 3.7 enforcement entry, a TA6 answer that contradicts the survey
kinds.note: Enforcement is time-limited (4 years / 10 years, now 10 for most breaches) — an indemnity is available only if the authority has not been approached.
actions: Establish the date of the works and the enforcement window
Decide indemnity versus retrospective consent BEFORE approaching the authority

kinds.label: Building-regs approval missing
kinds.arisesFrom: an extension, loft, knocked-through wall, new boiler or windows with no completion certificate / FENSA / Gas Safe
kinds.note: One of the most common hold-ups. Lenders accept an indemnity or a regularisation certificate, but some insist on regularisation for structural or recent work; an indemnity needs lender approval (days to weeks).
actions: Ask for the completion certificate / FENSA / Gas Safe
Quote an indemnity or a regularisation certificate
Report to the lender; some insist on regularisation

kinds.label: Search adverse entry
kinds.arisesFrom: a search result the client or lender needs to act on: flood risk, contaminated land, a road scheme, a chancel liability, a mining report, no public sewer connection
kinds.note: Flood risk must be reported to the lender, who may withdraw; insurability is the practical test.
kinds.overlaps: the search sub-flow raises the flag as a decision; the issue tracks what the decision started (a further report, the lender's view)
actions: Read the entry against the property
Obtain a specialist report or an indemnity
Report to the lender where required (flood)

kinds.label: Search delayed
kinds.arisesFrom: a local authority running weeks behind, a provider outage, a search that has to be re-ordered for freshness
kinds.note: Search indemnity insurance is the usual workaround when a council is slow and the lender allows it.
kinds.overlaps: the search wait timer chases at day 10 and escalates at day 18; raise the issue when the delay changes the plan (indemnity, new target dates)
actions: Consider search indemnity if the lender allows

kinds.label: Enquiry unanswered
kinds.arisesFrom: the other side has gone quiet: the seller's solicitor has not replied, or has replied to everything but the one that matters
kinds.note: The "enquiry stalemate" is the forum staple: weeks of "we are waiting for our client".
kinds.overlaps: the enquiry wait timer chases at day 5 and escalates at day 15
actions: Chase the seller's solicitor in writing

kinds.label: Unsatisfactory enquiry response
kinds.arisesFrom: "the buyer must rely on their own survey / searches", a refusal to give a statement of truth, an executor who will not answer
kinds.note: Executors and attorneys legitimately cannot answer TA6 questions; the client is advised and decides.
kinds.overlaps: the enquiry sub-flow flags partial / refused replies as a decision; "request further" raises a tracked follow-up
actions: Obtain the evidence another way (search, indemnity)
Advise the client and record their decision

kinds.label: Source-of-funds evidence outstanding
kinds.arisesFrom: a gifted deposit not declared early, an inheritance, crypto or overseas funds, savings with no paper trail
kinds.note: The single most common self-inflicted delay: the gift is mentioned late and the donor is elderly or abroad; the lender must be told of a gift too.
actions: Record the MLRO's view for EDD cases

kinds.label: AML / KYC problem
kinds.arisesFrom: a referred or failed electronic check, a PEP or sanctions hit, an ID that will not verify, a client abroad who cannot be met
kinds.note: Enhanced due diligence is a compliance decision; the matter cannot progress to money moving without it.
kinds.overlaps: the ID/AML sub-flow flags the provider result as a decision; rejecting it halts automation

kinds.label: Mortgage offer outstanding
kinds.arisesFrom: the application is stuck: underwriting queries, a valuation not yet booked, a broker waiting on documents
kinds.note: Nothing exchanges without the offer; the chain waits.
kinds.overlaps: mortgage.status = awaiting already blocks pre_contract; the issue is where the handler records why
actions: Establish what the underwriter is waiting for

kinds.label: Mortgage condition outstanding
kinds.arisesFrom: a special condition on the offer: a retention, works, an occupier's consent, an indemnity approval, insurance, proof of deposit
kinds.note: Exchange with an unsatisfied condition risks funds not being released on the day.
kinds.overlaps: the mortgage sub-flow flags each special condition as a decision
actions: Satisfy the condition and report to the lender
Confirm the lender is content before exchange

kinds.label: Mortgage offer expiring
kinds.arisesFrom: the offer's expiry date closing in on a matter that is not ready to exchange
kinds.note: Lenders extend once, sometimes twice, for a few weeks; a re-issue means re-underwriting on today's rates.
kinds.overlaps: the deadline timer raises this 15 working days out; the issue tracks the extension request
actions: Determine the extension requirements and timing
Plan exchange and completion inside the offer, or start a re-issue

kinds.label: Mortgage offer expired
kinds.arisesFrom: the offer lapsed before exchange
kinds.note: A fresh application, valuation and offer; rates may have moved.
kinds.overlaps: record mortgage_offer_withdrawn (the sub-flow reopens and blocks exchange); the issue tracks the re-application
actions: Tell the chain the timetable has moved

kinds.label: Valuation issue
kinds.arisesFrom: a down-valuation below the agreed price, a valuer's retention or "further reports required" (roof, damp, timber), a nil valuation (spray foam, cladding, knotweed)
kinds.note: Options are renegotiate, make up the shortfall, a fresh valuation with another lender, or a challenge; a price change must be reported to the lender and can change the offer.
actions: Get the valuation figure and the reason
Renegotiate, top up, challenge, or move lender
Report a price change to the lender

kinds.label: Lender approval needed
kinds.arisesFrom: anything the lender must be told: a price change, an indemnity policy, a retention, flood risk, a change of circumstances
kinds.note: Raised automatically by the machine when a price change or an indemnity resolution needs the lender's confirmation; days to weeks in practice.
actions: Report to the lender through the panel portal
Chase for confirmation the offer stands

kinds.label: Deposit issue
kinds.arisesFrom: a deposit below 10%, a deposit funded by the sale in a chain, a deposit not yet in cleared funds, a gifted deposit not yet evidenced
kinds.note: A reduced deposit needs the seller's agreement in the contract; a deposit "up the chain" is normal but must be agreed.
actions: Agree a reduced deposit or a deposit up the chain in the contract

kinds.label: Completion funds shortfall
kinds.arisesFrom: the client balance is short of the completion statement: SDLT underestimated, a bonus or ISA not yet released, a sale proceeds shortfall in the chain
kinds.note: Before exchange it is a plan; after exchange it is a completion failure in waiting.
actions: Establish where the shortfall is coming from and evidence it
Warn the chain if completion may move

kinds.label: Lender funds delayed
kinds.arisesFrom: the advance not released: the certificate of title sent late, a condition unsatisfied, the lender's cut-off missed
kinds.note: Most lenders need the COT 5 working days before completion; a late advance means late completion interest.
kinds.overlaps: the funds wait timer chases the lender from day 2
actions: Check the certificate of title and the conditions

kinds.label: Chain dependency
kinds.arisesFrom: the top or bottom of the chain is not ready: their management pack, their enquiries, their buyer pulled out, their mortgage
kinds.note: Agents say "ready" a week before solicitors are; a link dropping out costs ~10 weeks; the collapse is often discovered on exchange day.
actions: Get the chain position from the agents
Confirm with the solicitors, not the agents

kinds.label: Seller delay
kinds.arisesFrom: the seller has not returned the protocol forms, signed the contract, provided documents, or instructed their solicitor on a point
kinds.note: The commonest reason a matter sits: nothing is technically wrong, someone is just not doing it.

kinds.label: Buyer delay
kinds.arisesFrom: our own client: survey not booked, documents not returned, the deposit not sent, the mortgage application not made
kinds.note: Record it so the file shows who was waiting for whom.
actions: Tell the client what is waiting on them and by when

kinds.label: Third-party consent required
kinds.arisesFrom: a landlord's licence to assign, a management company's consent, a chargee's consent to a transfer, a Help to Buy redemption / consent, a shared-ownership provider
kinds.note: Third parties work to their own clock and fee; a Help to Buy redemption needs a RICS valuation and 4–6 weeks.
actions: Apply for the consent with the fee

kinds.label: Document execution problem
kinds.arisesFrom: a deed signed but not witnessed, a witness who is a party, a wrong name, an electronic signature the other side or HMLR will not accept, a signatory abroad
kinds.note: Re-execution is the only fix and takes as long as the post takes.

kinds.label: Occupier consent required
kinds.arisesFrom: an adult occupier (partner, adult child, lodger) who must sign a consent / deed of postponement for the lender
kinds.note: A standard mortgage condition; the occupier is advised separately.
actions: Have the consent signed with separate advice

kinds.label: Probate issue
kinds.arisesFrom: the grant not yet issued, executors not all signing, an intestacy, a sale by a personal representative before the grant
kinds.note: Everything but exchange can proceed before the grant; the grant itself can take 12 weeks to many months.
actions: Confirm the grant has been applied for and the expected date

kinds.label: Power-of-attorney issue
kinds.arisesFrom: an LPA not registered, a donor whose capacity is in doubt, an attorney signing beyond their authority, an unregistered general power
kinds.note: HMLR and lenders want the registered LPA (or certified copy) and evidence it is still valid.
actions: Obtain the registered LPA / certified copy

kinds.label: Bankruptcy / insolvency issue
kinds.arisesFrom: a K16 bankruptcy search hit against the buyer, a seller with a bankruptcy restriction on the title, a company seller in liquidation
kinds.note: A hit against a borrower stops the lender; a trustee in bankruptcy must sign for an insolvent seller.
actions: Establish whether the hit is our client

kinds.label: Survey defect
kinds.arisesFrom: the client's survey (damp, roof, subsidence, electrics, asbestos, timber, knotweed, spray foam)
kinds.note: Most renegotiations settle at 1–5% off; lenders may impose a retention (knotweed, spray foam); the seller may refuse and the buyer walks.

kinds.label: Environmental risk
kinds.arisesFrom: environmental / flood / mining / radon reports the client and lender must accept
kinds.note: Flood risk must be reported to the lender, who may withdraw; insurability is the practical test.

kinds.label: Third-party arrangement
kinds.arisesFrom: a solar-panel roof lease, a septic tank (general binding rules), overage, a s.106, a rentcharge, a guarantee that must be assigned
kinds.note: A solar lease must be assignable and lender-acceptable; a non-compliant septic tank must be replaced or the price reflect it.

kinds.label: Document missing
kinds.arisesFrom: FENSA / gas / electrical certificates, guarantees, the EPC, planning decision notices the seller cannot find
kinds.note: Often ends in a cheap indemnity or acceptance; sometimes the first sign of a bigger regs problem.

kinds.label: Disclosure concern
kinds.arisesFrom: TA6 answers that contradict the survey or searches, an undisclosed neighbour dispute, a complaint history, a death at the property
kinds.note: Misrepresentation exposure after completion; further enquiries first, then advice.

kinds.label: Completion failure
kinds.arisesFrom: lender funds late, the CHAPS cut-off missed, chain money not through, keys not released, a removal van on the drive and no money
kinds.note: Late-completion interest under the standard conditions; a notice to complete if it slips further.
actions: Agree the new time / date with the other side

kinds.label: Further investigation recommended
kinds.arisesFrom: the survey (or a specialist report) recommends a further specialist investigation before exchange: damp, timber, drainage, structural, electrical, roof
kinds.note: Raised automatically from the survey facts, one per recommendation. A specialist report that finds nothing resolves it (a fact); the client's satisfaction with the property is a separate client decision.
actions: Instruct the specialist named by the surveyor
File the report when it arrives (it is read automatically)
Put the outcome to the client

kinds.label: Other
kinds.arisesFrom: anything else the handler needs the matter to wait for

resolutions.label: price reduced
effects: records price_changed (new price required, before exchange only)
lender-funded purchase: raises a lender_approval issue holding exchange

resolutions.label: retention agreed
effects: lender-funded purchase: raises a lender_approval issue holding exchange

resolutions.label: works done by the seller before exchange
indemnity policy obtained
effects: lender-funded purchase: raises a lender_approval issue holding exchange

resolutions.label: new lender / fresh valuation
effects: lender-funded purchase: records mortgage_offer_withdrawn (the sub-flow reopens)

resolutions.label: insolvency cleared (trustee / discharge / not our client)
deposit arrangement agreed in the contract
client accepts as is (advised in writing)
